name: Suzanna McGee
quote:
Last year, I was 51 years old and I decided that I wanted to learn a handstand. That's how I found GymnasticBodies. Until this point, I never thought that I would want to do any gymnastic movements. The Handstand course was excellent. I am an athlete and a performance coach so I could really appreciate the depth of the program and the knowledge put into it.  

In the beginning of my training, I was very humbled. I thought that I was a pretty good athlete, but the programs quickly revealed many of my weaknesses. At first, I was "in a hurry" to quickly learn a handstand, but then I realized that this is going to be a long journey. I surrendered and started to train with the mindset that this is a lifestyle, where I am correcting all weaknesses and making the body strong from all angles—working on strength and mobility at the same time. The coaches are amazing and extremely helpful. It's almost like going to school on how to become a super human. Sometimes the progress seems very slow, but looking back, it has been a solid, continuous progress. I am not in a hurry anymore, this is the way to live.

name: James Jones
quote:
Hey! I've been following the foundation and stretch courses for just over 2 years now and I just want to thank you for putting together such an awesome course.

In the before pic I'd been doing Crossfit for 7 years, and dealing with a nagging back pain which eventually turned into a pretty devastating injury.

The after picture is 2 years of GB foundation, and thanks to you guys I'm pain free!

name: Roland Schoemann
quote:
Hi, my name is Roland Schoemann. I am a South African Olympian. I've represented my country at four Olympics and won three Olympic medals, including a gold. I'm a ten time World Record Holder and I'm a very, very humble GymnasticBodies subscriber.

I've been using the program now for a year and that first week had me realizing that I was in for an absolutely terrifying new challenge. As a swimmer, just the weighted mobility work to lengthen out my hamstrings was significant. There was so much disfunction in my hips and hamstrings…so it was by spending six months by working on that religiously and trying to loosen up that there's been a significant change in that muscle tone and I can actually feel the muscle being pliable again. It's not rock hard and it's not because it's a genetic defect or because that's how I'm destined to be  it's because I hadn't been doing enough of the right things to loosen up my hips and really work and loosen up my muscles the way they're meant to be.

Trying to figure out my thoracic extension has also been an incredible challenge and something that gets better on a daily basis. It's moving towards a weakness that is key and what I've been trying to embrace. What's important to understand is these exercises aren't easy, so embrace the fact that these are hard. The beauty of this is my understanding has grown. I spent 30 years putting my body into shortened position, into positions that aren't ideal – and to expect that these changes will take place overnight? That's not reality and something I remind myself of every day. Change is going to take more than a year. It could be a lifetime to put in the changes. You see all these amazing people doing handbalancing, touching the floor and doing presses. Did that just happen overnight? Probably not. So you have to embrace your weaknesses because that's how you're going to get better at them.

When you look at sports and specifically swimming, you can see mobile you need to be, how flexible you need to be, how dynamic you need to be and also relax. To me when I look at gymnasts, and you see the mobility, the strength, their ability to flow it's so much fluidity and so much relaxation. Then I started being really puzzled by wanting to be stronger. And the stronger I got it didn't make me faster.

Guys, my name is Roland Schoeman and I'm here on this journey with you. I'm starting this and have started this at the beginning like many of you have. Be encouraged by the fact that even Olympic Gold Medalists, even the best in the world have weaknesses and struggles. It was a fortuitous encounter with GymansticBodies, but it's glad I'm one that was made.

name: Andrey Trium
quote:
I started my journey back in 2009 when I reached my "peak" at 103kg. I am 76kg now (off 27kg!). One can imagine the Glory Road wasn't easy or straight: I have tried many fitness programs and eating styles to get where I am now. And, just like in many things in life, I discovered that the process was more important (and enjoyable!) than the result.

While Tim Ferriss eventually took care of my eating style, most of the fitness programs I have tried were based around doing more of the same: more kilos, more reps etc. Until I came across GST. GymnasticBodies training is about doing more of more: conquering you own body and your own mind, doing exercises you could not even dare thinking about, literally building your own body of your dreams. The keyword of Gymnastics Training is Mobility: a synergetic combination of Strength and Flexibility. Progressions is how you get there when somebody with years of experience takes care of your programming - and I think the follow-along videos are just a stroke of genius! Now, it is all about freedom: freedom of move, freedom of life!

Great and well balanced looks come as a nice bonus.

name: Ryan Bailey
quote:
I started this 1 year ago all concerned about how long things take to improve.  Things have changed...

I no longer care about time frames.

Thought I'd share a picture of some improvement from riding out the wave of consistent, enjoyable practice. Grateful for the stretch series and Coach Sommer's message of patience.

Better than I ever thought for myself.

(Top corner pic: December 2015): All stretched out, max range after Middle Split Stretch series. At the time, I was happy to finally be able to sit comfortably with legs in straddle without my hip flexors and abs cramping)

(Large pic: December 2016) A morning warm-up, not after a stretch session)

name: Jin Liu
quote:
I grew up failing half of my PE classes. I couldn't even do a pushup. Maybe I'm not born with speed or power, but with hard work and consistency, I managed to change that. I started working out 5-6 years ago with general conditioning, but something was lacking as I tried to learn some more advanced skills. I kept injuring my joints. I'm glad I found GymnasticBodies.

Over the past year, GymnasticBodies has helped me grow tremendously in terms of discovering my imbalances, developing strength and mobility, and even gaining knowledge about human body physiology. More importantly, its progressive approach has taught me patience, and how to build a solid foundation with the basics.

• I achieved my short-term goal of doing a strict and slow ring muscle up

• My joints are much stronger and more mobile than before

• My nagging pain from a hamstring injury two years ago is completely gone!

With GB, this is only a start of an amazing journey.

name: KC
quote:
Every single day, like clockwork, you can find our friend KC up there at 71-years-young, outside, keeping active and loving life. Most often he's rock climbing at the crag near his home in Arizona, but if his arms need a rest – he's out ripping single track on his mountain bike, playing tennis, skiing, or out for a recovery hike.

Gymnastic Strength Training is KC's base – one that he doesn't skip out on because it's critical to the hobbies that kept him feeling young and experiencing life to the absolute fullest. He also knows that his mobility training is critical to promote his recovery, setting him up and prepping him for the next adventure.
